clue.text: Comic writer's unhappiness about Dutch Royal family

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the writer to the wordplay

indicators.note: about means wrapped round, so the word for unhappiness goes round the Dutch abbreviation

parts.note: woe is misery or unhappiness
a royal dynasty is a house, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: A comic author grumbles about the Dutch royals.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the writer equals what follows. P. G. Wodehouse wrote the Jeeves and Wooster comic novels.
explanation.definitionFit: P. G. Wodehouse is the celebrated English humorist behind Jeeves and Wooster.

clue.text: Scottish pottery our group brought on my ship

parts.note: we is the group that includes us
SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: Our party brought Scottish pottery aboard my vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Wemyss Ware is a Scottish pottery from Fife, known for painted cabbage roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Wemyss Ware is decorated earthenware made in Kirkcaldy, Fife, from the 1880s.

clue.text: On the back foot, finally abandoning sailor after baton's whirled

indicators.note: after puts the shortened sailor behind the whirled baton
whirled means spun round, so the baton word is turned backwards

parts.note: a rod is a baton; the 's is 'is', joining it to whirled

indicators.note: abandoning means the end of foot is dropped from the sailor's word

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of foot

explanation.surface: Wrong-footed, with a sailor gone after a twirled baton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the back foot' is an idiom, but only 'On the back' defines; 'foot, finally' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorsal is the anatomical term for something situated on the back, like a dorsal fin.

clue.text: Hot desire in couple

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
an itch is a restless longing or desire

explanation.surface: A burning passion felt by a pair of lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' looks like a noun, a pair, but is the verb to join.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch is to fasten or join together, as a trailer is hitched to a car.

clue.text: Liberal apprehended by one in the dark

indicators.note: apprehended by means the Liberal letter is caught and held inside the word for one

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: A Liberal arrested by someone at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehended' looks like 'understood', fitting 'in the dark', but here means arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without lighting, so a place left unlit is dark.

clue.text: A European upset about most of pepper in Mexican dish

indicators.note: about means the reversed pair wraps around the shortened pepper
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a Dane is a European, from Denmark

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the pepper word is dropped

parts.note: a chili is a hot pepper

explanation.surface: A distressed European fusses over a pepper in a Mexican meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so the reversal reads upwards; 'about' wraps it round the shortened pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican tortilla rolled round a filling and baked in chilli sauce.

clue.text: Excellent Old English writer

parts.note: def is slang for excellent or cool

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine author from the age of Old English literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old English writer' reads as one phrase, but Old English is wordplay and 'writer' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the novelist who wrote Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Dutch produce line in skilful fight with English

indicators.note: in means the line letter sits inside the skilful word

parts.note: deft means skilful
war is fighting or a fight

explanation.surface: A Dutch product line, skilfully made, fighting the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining war and English.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is the blue-and-white tin-glazed pottery made in Delft in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Ranger, perhaps, in favour of development of trees

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in voting for

indicators.note: development means the letters of trees are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A park ranger backing tree planting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' says a ranger is one example of a forester.
explanation.definitionFit: A forester manages woodland, and a forest ranger is one kind of such a worker.

clue.text: Bridge opponents, in boring style, overlooking some altogether

parts.note: in bridge East and North sit at adjacent seats and are opponents

indicators.note: overlooking means passing over, so the word some is dropped from the boring adverb

parts.note: tiresomely means in a boring way

explanation.surface: Card players at the bridge table, bored, ignoring some of the hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points; E and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely means wholly or completely, the sense of altogether.

clue.text: After a switch, describing fighting for the Union?

indicators.note: a switch means two neighbouring letters change places in the word for describing fighting

parts.note: martial describes war or combat, as in martial arts

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether a fighting word can be about the Union in a civil war.
explanation.walkthrough: In MARTIAL the T and I swap places. 'Union' looks like a political or military union but here means marriage; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage, the union of two spouses.

clue.text: Criminal pair I found in religious group

indicators.note: found in means the pair and I are located inside the religious group's word

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect or group

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer and an accomplice discovered inside a religious sect.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person guilty of an offence, an offender.

clue.text: Food breaks rejected? It will be reviewed after the riots

indicators.note: after places the reviewed word behind the riotous one
rejected means sent back, so the word for breaks is read backwards

parts.note: gaps are breaks or pauses

indicators.note: riots means the letters of the word just before run wild and are rearranged
reviewed read as re-viewed, looked at the other way, so the word is turned around

explanation.surface: Rejected food breaks will be looked at again after unrest in the canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riots' looks like part of the story but is the anagram signal for 'the'; 'reviewed' is read as re-viewed, seen backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long thin Italian pasta, a staple food.

clue.text: Support retreating holding a weapon

indicators.note: holding means the reversed support word grips the article inside it
retreating means going backwards, so the word for support is reversed

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a snooker cue

explanation.surface: Backup falls back while one soldier keeps a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns REST into TSER, and 'holding' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a stun gun that fires electrified darts, a non-lethal weapon.

clue.text: Very distinctive versifier leading a saboteur into small room

indicators.note: into means the poet, a and saboteur are put inside the small room's word

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

indicators.note: leading means the versifier comes first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: Edward Lear was a writer of nonsense verse and limericks
a sab is a hunt saboteur, a protester who disrupts fox hunts

explanation.surface: A poet escorts a saboteur into a tiny room.
explanation.walkthrough: SAB is British slang for a hunt saboteur, an activist who disrupts fox hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear as a bell is an idiom for something perfectly distinct, heard or understood with no trouble.

clue.text: Toilet block's latest leak I repaired — it seems to be the same thing again

definitions.text: it seems to be the same thing again

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet

indicators.note: latest means the final letter of block is taken

parts.note: the 's shows the latest letter belongs to block

indicators.note: repaired means fixed, so the letters of leak and I are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A plumber fixes a toilet block's newest leak, which looks like the old one again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' looks like a plumber's job but signals rearranging LEAK I.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookalike is a person or thing closely resembling another, a double.

clue.text: Mystery writer completely exhausted regular appearances of Gothic axemen

parts.note: all in is an informal phrase for completely worn out

indicators.note: regular appearances means every third letter is picked from these words

explanation.surface: A crime novelist worn out by hordes of Gothic axe murderers.
explanation.walkthrough: The regular pick takes every third letter of GOTHIC AXEMEN, starting at G.
explanation.definitionFit: Margery Allingham was a detective novelist of the golden age, creator of Albert Campion.

clue.text: Gloomy flower? Hoped lass not wholly distressed

indicators.note: distressed means upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder
not wholly means the last letter of lass is left off

explanation.surface: A girl's hopes are dashed in a sad garden.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the asphodel covers the Fields of Asphodel in the underworld, hence 'Gloomy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily linked with death and the underworld in Greek myth.

clue.text: Canine trainer's source of specialist goods

parts.note: C stands for a canine tooth in dental notation
a handler trains and controls an animal; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A dog trainer is the place to buy specialist kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine trainer' suggests a dog handler; it splits into C and HANDLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler is a dealer in specialist supplies, especially a ship's chandler selling marine equipment.

clue.text: Serve alcohol in error — this is an adolescent looking for work

indicators.note: in error means the letters of the preceding words are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A barman wrongly serves drink to an underage teenager hunting for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this is' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A school-leaver is a teenager just finishing school and starting out in employment.

clue.text: Cancel housing core of kennels in extension

indicators.note: housing means the cancel word holds the core inside it

parts.note: to axe a plan is to cancel it

indicators.note: core means the central letters of kennels

explanation.surface: Plans scrapped for housing dogs in a new wing.
explanation.walkthrough: The core is the middle three letters of KENNELS, NNE.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added on to a main one, an extension.

clue.text: Beer drunk? Inebriated, leaving court with a jaunty air

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of beer are jumbled
leaving means the word for court departs from the woozy word

parts.note: woozy means unsteady or tipsy
to woo is to court

explanation.surface: A tipsy drinker leaves the courtroom in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court but means woo, which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Breezy means lively and carefree in manner, cheerfully casual.

clue.text: Woman returned an Oriental shrub

parts.note: hen is informal for a woman, as in a hen party

indicators.note: returned means the little word an is read backwards

explanation.surface: A woman came back with an Asian bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman returned' reads like one person coming home, but 'returned' acts only on 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a flowering bush of Asia and North Africa whose leaves give a red-brown dye.

clue.text: Aristocrat and European prince I omitted? It should be easy to sort out

definitions.text: It should be easy to sort out

parts.note: nob is slang for a toff or aristocrat

indicators.note: omitted means the letter I is dropped from the prince's name

parts.note: Rainier III was the Prince of Monaco

explanation.surface: A toff and a Monaco royal, minus one, make a simple problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Rainier was a Prince of Monaco, husband of Grace Kelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is a decision or problem so simple it needs no thought.

clue.text: Painter foremost in British art study

indicators.note: foremost means the first letter of art is taken

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A painter at the forefront of British art studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an Irish-born British artist famed for his distorted figure paintings.

clue.text: Depiction of country sadly includes temperature

indicators.note: includes means the temperature letter goes inside the sad exclamation

parts.note: alas is a cry of sadness

explanation.surface: A drawing of a nation, regrettably featuring hot weather.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps showing the lands of the world.

clue.text: Part of London not totally boring, with attractive woman taking time out

indicators.note: not totally means the boring word loses its final letter

parts.note: dull means boring

indicators.note: time is T, and taking it out removes that letter from the word for an attractive woman

parts.note: a witch can mean a bewitching, enchanting woman

explanation.surface: A London suburb, not quite dull, where a charmer takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Dulwich is a leafy area of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulwich is a district in south London, known for its college and picture gallery.

clue.text: Place for student member in French school head abandoned

indicators.note: in means the member goes inside the beheaded school word
head abandoned means the first letter of the French school word is dropped

parts.note: école is French for school
a leg is a limb, and a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A student's place, with a member in a French school whose head has quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a headteacher who has gone; it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is an institution where students study for further or higher education.

clue.text: Substantial article carried in both hands, say, to be returned

indicators.note: carried in means the article is held between the letters for the two hands

parts.note: L and R are left and right, the two hands
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: to be returned means the abbreviation for say is read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: An item is carried in both hands, for example, to be sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is 'for example', EG, which 'to be returned' turns to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Large means big or considerable in size, which is what substantial means.

clue.text: American breaking into huge unknown religious building

indicators.note: breaking into means the American abbreviation forces its way inside the huge word

parts.note: monster as an adjective means huge, as in a monster sale
in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: An American bursts into a vast mysterious house of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is a building where monks live as a religious community.
